text.title: CR / BUG Tracking Core Rules
text.summary: 10 testable rules for the CR and BUG side-streams: file shape, lifecycle states, commit prefixes, global per-repo numbering, optional feature linkage, and the mandatory project-spec update when a BUG exposes a missing rule. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: A CR file MUST fit on one page (≤80 lines) and contain three sections: Why, What changes, Optional linked-feature.
rule.rationale: Keep it cheap. If the CR needs more, it is a feature.

rule.statement: CR moves through exactly two states: `crs/todo/` → `crs/done/`. No in-progress.
rule.rationale: CRs are short-lived. An extra state adds bureaucracy without surfacing anything new.

rule.statement: Commits implementing a CR MUST use prefix `cr(CR0NN): <short title>`.
rule.rationale: Lets release-notes generators split CR / BUG / FEATURE lines without parsing the body.

rule.statement: A BUG file MUST contain five sections: Symptom, Repro, Root cause, Fix, Regression test.
rule.rationale: Repro and root-cause are what distinguish a BUG from a CR — without them the fix is conjecture. The five-section file shape exists precisely so the test step cannot be skipped.
Repro work is real work; the in-progress state makes it visible to anyone scanning the queue.

rule.statement: Commits implementing a BUG fix MUST use prefix `fix(BUG0NN): <short title>`.
rule.rationale: Symmetric with `cr(CR0NN): ...`. Allows machine-grouped release notes.

rule.statement: The repo MAINTAINS exactly two global counters: one for CRs (`CR001`, `CR002`, …) and one for BUGs (`BUG001`, `BUG002`, …). CRs and BUGs do NOT share namespace.
rule.rationale: Separate counters make release notes legible: "Sprint shipped 3 features, 5 CRs, 2 BUGs" is meaningful only when the streams do not share IDs.

rule.statement: Counters are global per repo (NOT per feature, NOT per release). Numbers are never reused and the counter is never reset.
rule.rationale: Reuse would break grep-based history. Past IDs in commit messages must still resolve.

rule.statement: A CR or BUG MAY include a `linked-feature: F0NN` header to anchor it to the feature that introduced the surface in question.
rule.rationale: Aids "what shipped in F0NN — and what came back to bite us afterwards?" investigations.

rule.statement: If a BUG exposes an invariant or business rule that the project-spec did not capture, the fix PR MUST update `project-spec/business-rules.md` (and/or `project-spec/invariants.md`) in the same PR.
rule.rationale: The rebuild test depends on the spec being honest. A BUG that uncovered a missing rule is the cheapest moment to add it.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit a CR or BUG record passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when the work is a CR or BUG.

rule.statement: Skip; route to the feature lifecycle (change affects multiple subsystems or requires a task breakdown) or to a straight commit (one-line documentation tweak).
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when the work is neither a CR nor a BUG.
